title: The Deceiver
text: “So… where’s that Bitch princess?”
“She’s not here. I bet she’s back at the inn, doing some skin care under the guise of ‘preparing for tomorrow.’”

I’m seriously flabbergasted. By the way, I get the feeling that Lazy Pig is starting to suspect me. Well, if he does anything stupid, I’ll just have to take him out. The Lazy Pig’s survival skills are so impressive they’ll leave you speechless, so I’m sure he won’t do anything unnecessary. I’ve learned that the Lazy Pig is the type who won’t stir up trouble for the sake of his own safety.
“…That’s just like my older sister.”
“What a piece of shit. Anyway… I’ll give you credit for fighting off the attackers, but…”
“Oink oink…”
The Shadow Pig standing near my Finacée is muttering something under his breath.
“It’s a surprise that you showed up, but Motoyasu was even more shocked. So, who are you?”
“I’m a member of the kingdom’s intelligence unit. From the Queen’s faction, that is.”
The Shadow Pig gave a slight nod.
“I’ve come to advise you to head southwest.”
“Bub… Bubbuhi…”
The Shadow Boar is saying something, but I can’t make out what it’s saying. After that, my Father was exchanging a few words with the Shadow Boar.
“Spear Hero, wouldn’t you mind telling me just how much my sisters know about our movements?”
That’s the rare occasion my Finacée uses honorifics with me. It’s refreshing to notice that she’s speaking to me so bluntly while maintaining a subtle distance.
“Thanks to the Queen’s faction’s diversionary tactics, they’ve only got a rough idea of our general location.”
“She sure does talk a lot.”
It’s only natural that my Father harbors such strong hostility… but this isn’t the time to back down.
“I’ll give you credit for trying to save Motoyasu and the others. So, I just need to meet the Queen, right? Is that okay with Motoyasu, too?”
“That’s right. I have my own circumstances, so there’s a lot I can’t talk about, but O-to—Naofumi, I already know you’re not at fault for what’s happened so far.”
“…You’re almost suspiciously understanding.”

I could sense my father’s wariness rising even further. I have a vague feeling that if things continue like this, my Father won’t trust me, and things will take a turn for the worse. What should I do if Filo-tan orders an attack!?
“As for that issue, I’ll explain everything thoroughly once this incident is resolved.”
“Really?”
“Indeed. And… there’s something I can tell you now. I’ll explain the proper way to use the Legendary Weapons.”
Father’s eyebrows rose slightly. It seems that if things continue this way, there’s a high chance I’ll be able to gain his trust.
“The proper way to use it? I’ve already checked the help section.”
“I’m well aware that the help section is incomplete. That’s why I’m here to teach you… However, there’s a problem—if you don’t overcome it, you won’t be able to survive the grueling battles ahead.”
My Father began to look irritated by my slightly coy way of speaking. Still, it seems he’s willing to hear me out.
“Hmm…”

“To be honest, if Naofumi and the others would just come to a certain location in the southwestern part of Melromarc by a specific date, I could send them out of the country immediately. That part isn’t particularly difficult for us.”
“What? How would you do that?”

“Legendary Weapons can use the Portal Skill, you see. The government is well aware of that. Unfortunately, it’s precisely because they know Naofumi likely doesn’t possess one that they’re searching for him so frantically.”
My Father began to look as if he’d swallowed a bitter pill.
“Well, since we don’t know when pursuers might show up here, I suppose we’ll play it safe and send him to Zeltoble or Siltvelt or somewhere like that?”
“If we can go there, that’d probably be easier.”
“Bububu! Bububu!”
At this point, Kagebuta let out some frantic grunts at Father.
“Would it be a problem if we went to Siltvelt? If it is, I’d definitely want to go.”
“Well, if Naofumi, the Shield Hero, were to go to Siltvelt at this very moment and order the destruction of Melromarc, it would certainly lead to war.”
“Don’t say that so casually… Doesn’t that trouble you at all?”
“Unfortunately, it doesn’t bother me at all.”
It’s just that things are unfolding exactly as I expected, which is a bit of a problem. After all, my resolve to make the Crimson Swine pay for his deeds hasn’t changed.
“A Hero is supposed to have that much power, you know. I’m sure the Spear Hero must have connections with people in power—people quite different from my sister and father.”

My Finacée will back me up with my Father. You seem to have some misunderstanding here, don’t you? Well, it’s actually quite easy to curry favor with the Pig King, provided I offer him those pigs from Takt.

My Father is glaring at me with a look like he’s swallowed a bitter pill. I wonder why? Oh? In my head, my Father from the first world is saying, “Well, it’s because I realized I couldn’t make you suffer, isn’t it?”

I see! It’s true—back when I still believed in the Crimson Swine, whenever I’d get flustered or angry after his misdeeds were exposed, my Father seemed to be in a good mood. Since that’s no longer possible, I suppose that’s why he’s in a bad mood now.

Would he cheer up if I prostrated myself and licked his feet? It feels like that might just add fuel to the fire, so I’d better not do that. Father exhaled deeply once, as if to sort through his unpleasant feelings.
“If it were that easy to get to Siltvelt, I’d definitely want to go…”
“Wait a minute…”
My fiancée is looking at my Father with a troubled expression. My Father, in turn, looks at her with a blank expression.
“Mel-chan… Master, Filo, I don’t want to upset Mel-chan.”
“Naofumi-sama…”
“Yeah, yeah. It’s what Motoyasu says, after all. What good would it do to blindly trust him?”
My Father shrugged slightly and said this in a slightly mocking tone.
“Well then, shall we teleport to Zeltoble? I’m sure there won’t be any of the Three Heroes Church folks there.”
Though that does increase the chances of running into my Big Sister’s older sister.
“Go ahead and try it if you can. I’ll trust you just this once.”
With that, my Father agreed, so I invited him and the others to join my party. Of course, Crimson Swine had already been kicked out!
“Portal Spear!”
With a whoosh, I teleported my Father and the others to Zeltoble. Since Zeltoble is the City That Never Sleeps, we could hear the bustling crowds from afar.
“What’s this…?”
Big Sister let out a gasp of surprise.
“… Seriously…? Second Princess, are we really in Zeltoble?”
“Yes… This is Zeltoble, the capital of the nation of merchants and mercenaries. I’ve been here before.”
“Hmm? I can hear the sounds of a bustling city.”
“By the way, the wanted notice for the Shield Hero is only valid within Melromarc, so it’s safe to enter, right?”
“I don’t trust it that much. It’s just nice that we were able to get out of the country so easily.”
My father replied, sounding a bit wary. That’s strange… When I looped back again, my Father used to trust what I said a lot more.
“You must be exhausted from your life on the run, so I think it’d be best to follow the guide in the shadows over there to an inn.”
I’ll just let the pig—who’s under my Finacée’s command—show us the way. He should be able to handle things smoothly around here, after all.
“B… Bb…”
My Finacée’s subordinate, the pig, let out a troubled-sounding grunt but nodded.
“Does this mean you trust me a little more now?”
“…Alright. So, Motoyasu. What do you want from me?”

“I’ll have you transported to the southwestern region of Melromarc at the time I specify. From there, head toward the fortress to the southwest, and then it would be a great help if you’d engage me in combat.”
“Why?”
“To flush out the true enemy. Of course, it’s possible to defeat the true enemy elsewhere, but I’d prefer to take him down at that specific moment.”
“That’s a strangely vague way of putting it…”

Ugh… It’s incredibly frustrating. But it’s the safest course of action to ensure things go the way I want. Maybe I could rush straight into that scenario, but I don’t know what factors might get in the way. I want to avoid failing in this playthrough, the one where I got to meet Fleon-chan. Well… since I’ve already been told where the hermit is, I’ll probably be able to meet Fleon-chan anyway.
“Of course, I’ll pay you in advance for this favor. That’s how you use a weapon, after all.”
“…I’ll ask you this just in case.”
“You’ll probably say it’s impossible, but the proper way to use Legendary Weapons involves believing in them from the bottom of your heart. If you doubt them, you won’t be able to do it.”
“Then it’s impossible!”
Just as I expected, my Father answers that way. Well, considering what my past self did, I suppose it is difficult.
“But will that really let you overcome the grueling battles ahead?”
“Damn it… You’re making fun of me.”
My Father lets out a curse.
“Naofumi-sama…”
“Master? Spear Guy, if you bully Master, Filo won’t forgive you.”
Eek… Filo-tan is glaring at me! I really wish she’d stop.
“Wait, Filo-chan. The Spear Hero is just trying to help the Shield Hero in various ways. So, let’s wait a little while so the Shield Hero can prepare himself, okay?”

There seems to be some distance between my fiancée and my Father. She isn’t calling him by his name. As I recall… come to think of it, my Finacée usually refers to my Father as “The Shield Hero.” But this version of my Father is closer to how he was in the first world. Is it because of the time period?
“…Anyway, Motoyasu, I’m not saying I trust you, but tell me.”

My father has a hungry spirit when it comes to these matters, so he’s quick to cut to the chase. With that in mind, I briefly explained the basics to him—how to enhance the Four Holy Weapons, where to find them, and so on.
“Whether you can do it or not depends on Naofumi’s faith. Well then, I’ll come back another day.”
I raised my hand to bid my Father farewell, but he remained silent, still looking wary. So, I dropped my Father and the others off at the inn in Zeltoble and left the scene.

For the next few days, I’ll be caught up in a situation where the Three Heroes Church—who are trying to deceive my Father and tarnish the reputation of the Sacred Bird Saint—will be giving me a hard time. Now then… well. Since I know where they tend to show up, it might be a good idea for me to rush over there myself. However, since that would boost the Spear Hero’s reputation, it might be better to take a different approach.
“Naofumi and his group might be hiding in this town. Everyone, let’s split up and search!”
Seizing the moment, I’ll order the Crimson Swine to search the town with some words that sound good to their ears.
“Oink-oink! Oink!”

The Crimson Swine seem motivated, seeing this as a chance to eliminate their Finacée. I didn’t know anything back then, so I just accepted it as him caring deeply for his sister, but now I realize he was trying to kill her at the first opportunity. He really is a sickening pig.
“Alright! I’m heading this way!”

With that, I take off running at the crossroads, parting ways with the Crimson Swine, turn at a likely spot, and jump through a portal. My target is the place where the impostor posing as my Father is running amok. It seems he’d gone so far as to track down our location and was up to no good. He’s committing crimes in places we absolutely can’t reach.

Come to think of it, is there really any point in pulling off a diversion like this? From the Three Heroes Church’s perspective, it’s nothing short of foolish… but maybe it was an internal conflict or a crime committed by low-level members trying to cash in. Either way, I’m going to clear Father of these criminal suspicions.
“Duwah! That’s right!”
I put on the Filolial Mask I’d been hiding and headed toward the scene of the incident.
“Bubhee!”
“Hahahaha! I’m the Shield Hero!”

With that, a criminal—his face hidden by a mask and clad in armor and a shield modeled after the barbarian armor that my Father wears—was rampaging through the market stalls, ransacking merchandise. I encountered similar types back when my Father was stuck in Melromarc during that loop. But these copycat criminals are even more pathetic.
“Hold up! I say!”
“W-what!?”
I land on the roof of a house and shout at the criminal.
“I will not forgive anyone who commits evil where a saint’s great deeds lie, who ultimately frames the innocent, and who seeks to line their own pockets!”
“Who are you?! I’m the Demon of the Shield! State your name!”
“I have no obligation to tell a scoundrel like you, but I’ll make an exception!”
I spun my spear around and struck a pose reminiscent of the fierce Filolial-sama.
“Bird of the Colosseum! Filolial Mask has arrived!”
With a whoosh, I leap into the air and land right in front of the scoundrel impersonating my Father.
